Have you played League of Legends? Do you like league of legends but don't like pvp? This is the perfect game for you. Where you spend at least 35 minutes to re challenge a boss over and over again with two strangers or friends. 

The gameplay loop is okay up until hour 30, where you brain realizes the mundanity and annoyance it takes to fight a singeular nightlord. As someone who is employed and has to clean up after other people constantly, I don't have patience for a game that doesn't respect my time. This is one of those games that doesn't respect your time.

This is a major step down compared to Dark souls 2. The novelty of fighting dark souls bosses in this game wears off quickly when they aren't the end goal. An Elden ring boss is the end goal.

If you enjoy fighting Elden ring bosses, good for you. I loathe this new kind of boss fight Elden Ring has been going with. Where bosses constantly travel across the map, have outrageous health bars, 6+ hit multi combo attacks (including ones where they travel across the map), near blinding  vfx, and extremely short times to safely heal or attack the boss. Dark souls 3 perfected the format in my eyes, and they ruined it with their idea's in Elden ring.

This game doesn't respect the players time. After nearly 70 hours of gameplay, I still haven't unlocked every garb, and got maybe 4 or 5 god roll relics. 

It sucks spending 35 minutes on a run, to fight a nightlord, only to lose over and over again. Out of the 8 bosses, only one of which I fought, had I felt joy in beating. The other 7 I was relieved the pain was finally over.

If you like Leauge of Legends, love Elden ring, any rogue like game, and battle royal games, you will very likely at least enjoy this game. I yearn for fromsoft to go back the DS3 format of boss fights and their fairness, but I know that will never happen with the wild success of Elden ring.

Here is a review for the stubborn solo players. The $40 price tag for this one-of-a-kind, co-op Elden-Souls bonanza is a little high for never setting foot in multiplayer, but if you enjoy FromSoft bosses and are in the mood for learning a completely new format, you may find the price to be just fine. Nightreign introduces new mechanics through its characters' unique abilities, including a spell system revolving around combining elements, an improved ranged combat experience, a grappling hook, and a Sekiro parry. The new boss fights, as usual, are visually stunning, and the game is challenging enough to keep you busy for many hours. Despite all of this, it is easy to understand why many players are left disappointed with their first experience with this game. 

[b]"Is single player fun?"[/b]

It's difficult to get the hang of Nightreign, as no amount of experience from past games can prepare you for the blazing pace at which you need to move through the map, and only online guides or experience can provide you with the underlying knowledge that you need to plan your route.  In my opinion, even if you adore FromSoft boss fights, this game can only be enjoyable after learning how to keep up in levels. Learning how to play this game organically is a long, painful process of trail and error as you memorize each type of location on the map, gradually piece together a list of priorities, and develop your sixth sense for when the circle is about to close (for which there is no in-game timer!). Nightreign presents a varied cast of playable characters, but unfortunately some are noticeably better suited for solo play than others due to factors such as inherent tankiness, lower reliance on equipment drops, high poise damage, or being able to consistently DPS at range. As a result, you may feel that some characters are off limits until you become more experienced. The bosses feel like they have higher stakes than their source games because of the time commitment to reach them. As a person who hasn't completed Elden Ring, I personally found most returning bosses to be more difficult than the Night Lords, and there are a few that I fully resign to losing to when they show up as a night boss. The inability to retry the fights makes the bosses more frustrating than in Elden Ring or Dark Souls, where you can quickly try again. To make things worse, you will have no teammates that can help you by splitting aggro. The steep learning curve (or "knowledge wall?"), constant decision-making, spreedrun mentality, and high stakes boss fights lead to a high-intensity experience that inspires feelings of both frustration and exhilharation. If you plan to avoid guides, you will need to approach this game with a substantial amount of patience and tolerance for failure while you figure out a plan of attack. If you are in the mood for this type of experience, you can expect to have fun.

[b]Solo Scaling:[/b]

As I am sure you are aware, Nightreign was designed as a 3-player co-op experience and was quickly criticized for being too difficult for solo. Within a week of release, single player mode was patched to add one free revive per night boss and increase the acquisition of runes, which are used for levelling up and buying items from merchants. These changes made soloing more feasible for the average player. Bosses in single player mode have much lower poise and their health is reduced to 1/3. Vendors are also guaranteed to sell a rare self-revive item, such that it is easy to end up with 3 self-revives when fighting the Nightlord at the end of each expedition. As far as I am aware, everything else is the same. You may often feel like there too many enemies around due to everything being designed for three players, but, thankfully, only one or two enemies will actively attack you at once. At the time of this review, there appears to be a healthy mix of opinions regarding the difficulty (or lack thereof) when playing solo.

[b]My recommendation for trying the game within the 2-hour Steam refund window:[/b]

If you're looking to form an opinion on the game within 2 hours, I strongly recommend looking up guides and possibly watching speed runs to learn how to effectively plan your route. Unfortunately, exploring the locations at your own pace in this short time is likely to result in you being underlevelled, which will greatly dampen your experience. As a new player, you will not know which locations are reasonable for you to tackle in the earlier vs later parts of the run, and it will take trial and error to gauge the difficulty of each location. At least one of your runs should be with a character that can solo well (Wylder, Raider, Ironeye, and maybe Executor if you're good at Sekiro) because the difference in difficulty is night and day. A successful run will take around 45 minutes, so consider trying one of these right off the bat. In my opinion, the boss pool in the first expedition is the most difficult, and I also found the first Nightlord to be more difficult than most of the others for solo. So, please do not feel discouraged if you struggle with them, I promise it gets easier!
